situation:
You are the marketing manager for GREENFOLD PACKAGING, which makes compostable takeout containers and sells them to restaurants, hotels and resorts across this state. GREENFOLD PACKAGING leads the region here and is now opening in the state next door, where it holds no accounts at all. The vice president (judge) has put you on the job of landing the first hundred customers there.

The largest tourism county in that state is expected to vote next spring on banning foam takeout containers. The vote has not been scheduled and nobody can say how it will go. If it passes, the hotels and resorts there will need what GREENFOLD PACKAGING makes within a few months. If it does not, those accounts come one kitchen at a time, the way they came here.

One course is to lease a warehouse in that state on a two-year term, staff its receiving dock, and train a crew to unload, inspect and log incoming pallets under the same safety precautions the home warehouse follows. Customers get two-day delivery and a service the sales team can sell alongside the product. The lease and the payroll are owed whether or not the foam vote passes.

The other course is to serve the new state from the home warehouse through NORTHLINE FOODSERVICE SUPPLY, a regional distributor already calling on those hotels. There is no lease and no crew to pay for, but the distributor takes half the margin, owns the customer relationship, and can put a competing container on the same truck. The board's expansion funds cover one course or the other, not both.

The vice president (judge) has asked you to recommend which course brings in the first hundred customers, and to explain how GREENFOLD PACKAGING should market itself in the new state either way. The vice president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president (judge) of GREENFOLD PACKAGING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

This is the company's first move outside its home state and you have one pool of expansion funds to spend on it. You want the marketing manager's recommendation on whether to lease the warehouse and staff its receiving dock or to sell through NORTHLINE FOODSERVICE SUPPLY, and how the company should be marketed there.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it was not?
